 UAE Launches World-First Integrated Digital Platform for Tourist VAT Refunds
 Oct 21, 2026 
 UAE Launches World-First Integrated Digital Platform for Tourist VAT Refunds
 The Federal Tax Authority has introduced an integrated digital platform for Value Added Tax refunds to tourists, describing it as the first of its kind globally, according to TradeArabia News Service . The authority said the launch supports its strategy of widening the use of digital technologies, improving the efficiency of its operating systems and advancing initiatives under the Digital Zero Bureaucracy Programme. 
 The platform was launched in cooperation with Planet , the authorised operator of the VAT Refund Scheme for Tourists. It is designed to provide a fully digital, paperless refund process for tourists, covering verification and data entry through an enhanced mobile application alongside facial recognition technology. The system is now operating at Zayed International Airport in Abu Dhabi, Dubai International Airport and Sharjah International Airport.
 Launch events at Zayed International Airport and Dubai International Airport were attended by senior officials, including Lieutenant General Mohammed Ahmed Al Marri, Director General of the General Directorate of Identity and Foreigners Affairs in Dubai; Abdulaziz Mohammed Al Mulla, Director General of the Federal Tax Authority; Sultan Al Dhaheri, Senior Vice President for Operations at Abu Dhabi Airports; Majed Al Joker, Chief Operating Officer of Dubai; Jorg Oppermann, Acting Chief Operations Officer at Abu Dhabi Airports; and Malek Al Madani, Executive Director of Government Services Quality Monitoring and Community Engagement.
 Al Mulla said the platform represents a significant step in the tourist tax refund process and reflects a government model centered on service design for customers, supported by data-sharing between government entities and partners. He indicated that the authority has accelerated refund procedures as part of its digital zero-bureaucracy efforts, noting that as of October 2026 the total time for tourists to receive VAT refunds had been reduced to one business day from approximately nine days previously.
 He added that the reduction in refund time and the new platform build on earlier achievements, including the introduction of a fully digital tourist tax refund system several years ago and the launch of a VAT refund system for tourists' e-commerce purchases made during their stay in the country. According to the report, the authority said these initiatives support the development of government operations and the reduction of bureaucracy in public services.
